correctness.rationale: For length t, y+2z=u=n-at and x=t-u+z, so max(0,u-t)<=z<=floor(u/2). At n0=(a+1)(a+2) through n0+a-1 the possible lengths are a+2,a+3 and, at the stated ends, a+1 or a+4. Summing their counts gives (2), at most p in both parities. Adding an a-coin injects representations along each residue class, extending the bound to all smaller positive n. At m=n0+a the three contributions 2,k+2,2 give k+6. For c=m+2, the totals at c and c+2 in the even case are k+6,k+5, and the totals at c-1,c,c+1 in the odd case are k+6,k+6,k+5. The possible lengths there are a+2 through a+4, including at a=7. Cofiniteness follows by adding any representable n-m to each representation of m, and the same injection gives closure. Any generator other than m is in its Apéry set, so e<=m. If equality held, every nonzero Apéry element would be a generator, in contradiction to the decomposable sum u+v whose predecessor u+v-m is a gap. Separately, I enumerated (y,z) and then all admissible n for eight a values of both parities from 7 to 32, and checked full finite generating sets using the conductor bound C=m+a²-1 and the fact that n>=C+m is decomposable.
